ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence on every director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner before incorporation: PEP screening against the Cyprus MOKAS/FIU PEP database and international PEP lists; sanctions screening against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, and UK HMT sanctions list; negative news and adverse media checks; source of wealth and source of funds verification; identity verification through independent official documents. The results must be documented, retained for at least five years after termination of the relationship, and made available to Cypriot obliged entities and competent authorities under Law 188(I)/2007.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: DRCIP e-Companies Portal - Department of Registrar of Companies and Intellectual Property, Republic of Cyprus; URL: https://efiling.drcor.mcit.gov.cy/drcipPortal/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed company name may be submitted in English and/or Greek. Names must appear in Latin transliteration in the registry index when submitted in Greek; the registered name must end with 'Ltd' or 'Limited'. The name cannot be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered name, cannot imply government patronage, and must comply with the Companies Law submission standards.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name clearance is valid for 180 days from issuance; if the company is not incorporated within that period, the name is released and a new clearance application is required. There is no automatic extension, but a new application may be filed for the same name if it remains available. Upon rejection, the applicant may request written reasons from the Registrar, submit a revised application with alternative names, or file an administrative recourse with the competent Administrative Court under Article 146 of the Constitution of the Republic of Cyprus within 75 days of notification. Tokens requiring prior approval must be supported by written consent from the appropriate regulatory authority before incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is administratively accepted for registration purposes where the service provider maintains a physical Cyprus street address and mail-handling capability. However, for a DTC cosmetics and beauty retail company using online payment rails, a pure virtual office will not by itself satisfy the economic substance expectations of the Cyprus Tax Department, financial institutions, or merchant acquiring banks. The company should maintain premises, equipment, operational staff, Cyprus-based board decisions, and core management presence to support tax residence and commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated annual risk of unannounced physical on-site inspection for this low-risk online retail activity is 5%-10%. The risk increases to approximately 15%-25% where the only registered presence is a virtual office, or where PEP/sanctions flags are present, or where the company applies for a Cyprus tax residency certificate.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: The Companies Law, Cap. 113 (Cyprus), as amended; primary provisions governing incorporation of private companies, memorandum and articles of association, registered office, share capital, appointment of directors and secretary, and statutory registers.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver, Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry, Republic of Cyprus (e-Registry portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form HE1 – Application for Registration of a Private Company, together with Form HE2 Declaration of Compliance and the signed Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required under Cypriot law; there is no escrow or pre-deposit requirement. The Company may register with a small issued share capital, e.g. a single ordinary share of €1, or adopt an authorized share capital of €2,000 divided into 2,000 ordinary shares of €1 each.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company acquire and register as its registered office the address located at [Street], Nicosia, Cyprus, and that the Memorandum and Articles of Association filed with the Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver are adopted. RESOLVED, that the authorized share capital of €2,000 be divided into 2,000 ordinary shares of €1 each, and that the subscriber subscribes for 1,000 issued ordinary shares fully paid at par. RESOLVED, that [Name], [Name] and [Name] be appointed as the first directors and [Name] as secretary, and that each director is authorized to open bank accounts, appoint the registered agent, and complete all ancillary filings to give full effect to incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Search and Official Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver – Companies Section, e-Registry portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a digital name reservation application through the DRC e-Registry stating the desired corporate name in English and Greek, the proposed business scope (online retail of cosmetics and personal care products), and the applicant's details. The Registrar verifies the proposed name against existing company names and business names for exact similarity and misleading association.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name in English and Greek
Certified copy of applicant's passport
Brief statement of proposed business objects
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused because of similarity or misleading character, the applicant may file a second-choice name immediately, request written reasons from the Registrar, or contest the refusal under the review mechanism prescribed by Cap. 113.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Execution and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public in Cyprus or Consular Officer of the Republic of Cyprus abroad
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association using the Cypriot statutory model and adapting it for a private limited company. The objects clause must specifically authorize e-commerce and online retail of cosmetics, personal care products, and beauty accessories without granting industrial manufacturing powers. Each subscriber must sign the constitutional documents before a notary; identity documents are certified by the notary, and executed copies are prepared for electronic scanning.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum of Association
Draft Articles of Association incorporating private company restrictions
Certified passport and proof of residential address of each subscriber
Consent to act as registered office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar or the preparing lawyer identifies drafting defects, the memorandum or articles must be amended and re-executed by the subscribers before a notary; no filing fee is lost if the correction is completed before formal submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Statutory Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver – e-Registry Filing Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the DRC e-Registry, complete Form HE1, upload the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association, Form HE2 Declaration of Compliance, name reservation certificate, consent of the registered office provider, and identity documents of proposed directors and the secretary. Pay the official state filing fee online, and retain the electronic submission receipt for all subsequent corporate governance filings.
required_dossiers: Form HE1 (Application for Registration of a Private Company)
Form HE2 (Declaration of Compliance)
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Name reservation certificate
Registered office address consent
Certified identity documents of subscribers, directors and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DRC issues a query or refusal, the applicant must respond within 14 days by uploading corrected documentation through the same e-Registry file. If the objection relates to the company name, submit a revised name and continue the same application before re-payment is triggered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Registered Office Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After successful review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation through the e-Registry. The authorized corporate services provider should obtain the certified electronic copy and, upon request, the physical original. Verify that the registered office address and company legal name exactly match the approved application, then deliver the certificate to the directors.
required_dossiers: Incorporation application electronic reference number
Proof of official fee payment
Approved name reservation certificate
Consent of registered office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains clerical errors in the company name, date, or registered office, the company may file a correction application with the Registrar; the Registrar will issue a corrected certificate without requiring a fresh incorporation process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Board Meeting and Establishment of Statutory Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors, Company Secretary, and the corporate services provider maintaining the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass a unanimous written resolution in accordance with the Articles. Approve the allotment of the subscriber shares, issue the share certificate, adopt the registered office, confirm the appointment of the first directors and secretary, and approve the opening of corporate bank and payment-service accounts, including the intended payment rails. Ensure the creation of the statutory registers of members, directors, secretary, and charges at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Minutes or written resolution of the first board meeting
Share certificates issued to subscribers
Register of members
Register of directors and secretary
Signed consent forms of directors and secretary
Pro-forma board resolution approving bank account and payment provider accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the statutory registers or share-allotment records are deficient, the board may pass a curative resolution approving the corrected allotment and register entries; the secretary must update the books and resubmit any relevant notification to the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Environmental and Fire-Safety Clearance Assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Labour Inspection, Cyprus Fire Service, Local Municipality or District Authority, and Department of Environment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the pure online retail operations under ISIC 4791 do not require an industrial manufacturing or processing license. Assess whether any physical storage, dispatch, or shop premises will be occupied in Cyprus. If premises are used, coordinate with the local municipality for any retail trade license, submit an application to the Cyprus Fire Service for a fire safety certificate if employee access or public access is contemplated, and complete an occupational safety and health risk assessment under the relevant Cypriot legislation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Lease or ownership title for the physical premises, if applicable
Fire safety evaluation request, if applicable
Occupational health and safety risk assessment
Waste and packaging management contracts for e-commerce dispatch activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality or Fire Service conditions clearance, remedy the stated structural, fire, or waste-management deficiencies within the compliance period and request re-inspection. If no premises are occupied, document the exemption and retain the assessment file at the registered office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for a pure online retailer; the Department of Industrial Development and Technology would only become relevant if cosmetic manufacturing or repackaging processing were added to the actual business operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating license is required for ISIC 4791 online retail of cosmetics and personal care products. A local municipal retail or trade license may be required only if a physical shop or warehouse is opened in Cyprus.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment, Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt: online retail does not fall within the EIA project categories under the Cypriot EIA Law L.127(I)/2018, so no Environmental Impact Assessment or preliminary environmental opinion is required for the standard e-commerce model.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, dust, or combustion emissions are generated. Any e-commerce warehouse must comply with municipal wastewater discharge limits, maintain separate collection of packaging waste under the Cyprus Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulations, and follow the applicable European waste classification and disposal requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety certificate is required for a pure administrative e-commerce office. If a physical shop or storage warehouse is established, a fire safety certificate from the Cyprus Fire Service is required, together with structural load verification for storage racks and an occupational risk assessment under the Occupational Safety and Health Law 89(I)/1996; the Department of Labour Inspection may conduct a workplace inspection before employment begins.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Tax Department of the Republic of Cyprus, Ministry of Finance; online e-filing portals: Ariadne VAT e-service and Tax Portal e-filing system (https://taxportal.mof.gov.cy).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Cyprus private limited company must first be incorporated and registered at the Registrar of Companies, obtaining its HE/Company Registration Number. The company is then required to complete registration with the Cyprus Tax Department within 60 days of incorporation or commencement of business, which results in the allocation of a Cyprus Tax Identification Code. VAT registration is a separate application submitted through the Ariadne VAT portal; registration is mandatory within 30 days after taxable supplies exceed EUR 15,600 over the preceding 12 months, or are expected to exceed that threshold in the following 30 days. Foreign entities without a fixed establishment may register as non-established taxable persons for VAT, and for cross-border B2C distance sales they may elect OSS or IOSS instead of a full local VAT registration where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Cyprus does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid classification election; a Cyprus Ltd is mandatorily treated as a separate entity-level taxpaying company. Available administrative elections include group loss surrender between 75% group companies, VAT group registration for closely related persons, and the qualifying IP box election. EU anti-hybrid mismatch rules apply and override arrangements designed to exploit classification differences; no elective hybrid-branch treatment is recognized.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Cyprus VAT Law 1991, transposing EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 15,600 annual taxable turnover in the preceding 12 months or expected in the next 30 days, calculated excluding VAT; for cross-border distance sales of goods into other EU Member States, the EU-wide B2C distance-selling threshold is EUR 10,000 per calendar year, while non-established suppliers have no local threshold when making taxable supplies considered to be located in Cyprus.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Cyprus does not currently impose real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory digital stamping, or tax-authority API validation for retail invoices. B2B and B2C e-invoicing is voluntary, except for public procurement B2G invoices, which must be e-invoiced through a PEPPOL-compliant solution. Taxpayers must issue valid VAT invoices, preserve their authenticity and integrity, and retain underlying export/customs records in accordance with the Cyprus VAT Law.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical export of goods from Cyprus to a non-EU destination qualifies for the 0% VAT rate when the goods are declared to Cyprus Customs, accepted for export, and removed from the customs territory evidencing by an approved export declaration and transport documentation. Intra-EU dispatches to another Member State may be zero-rated only where the purchaser's EU VAT number is valid, an EC Sales List is filed, and transport/removal evidence is retained. Input VAT attributable to exported goods remains recoverable through the Cyprus VAT return or refund procedure provided the export evidence package is maintained. Domestic B2C retail sales of cosmetics and personal care products to Cyprus consumers remain subject to the 19% standard rate; zero-rating does not depend on the online or DTC character of the seller.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Approved Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document) with Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Commercial invoice showing exporter, consignee, HS classification for cosmetics, quantities, price, Incoterms and payment terms
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or courier shipment manifest proving physical removal from Cyprus
Bank settlement evidence including SWIFT credit or Inward Remittance Certificate, supplemented by Shopify Payments/PayPal payout reports
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Cyprus Customs and the Tax Department may cross-check export declarations, MRN exit records, transport documents and banking/payment settlement evidence. Invalid or contradictory export substantiation may cause withdrawal of zero-rating, retrospective assessment at 19% VAT, statutory interest, monetary penalties for false declarations, and criminal prosecution for VAT evasion. The standard VAT assessment limitation period is generally six years, with an unlimited extension in cases of fraud or intentional wrongdoing. Retrospective clawback may also include denial of input VAT recovery and recharacterization of the supply as domestic retail VAT due in Cyprus.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Cyprus (Greek: Κεντρική Τράπεζα της Κύπρου), functioning within the Eurosystem and cooperating with the European Central Bank (ECB) under the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM) for significant credit institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Cyprus has adopted the euro (EUR) and maintains full current-account convertibility with no exchange-control approval requirement for trade or service transactions. The capital account is open to EU/EEA and third-country investors under Article 63 TFEU, subject to EU sanctions screening, AML/CFT controls, and BoP/IoP statistical reporting by banks. Profit remittance through dividends is unrestricted for non-resident shareholders and, subject to beneficial ownership documentation, no Cypriot dividend withholding tax applies to non-residents. Payment intermediaries must tag each wire with an EU BoP purpose code; mis-tagged or undocumented receipts may be rejected or suspended by the beneficiary bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory foreign-currency surrender requirement or mandatory conversion ratio applies to Cyprus exporters. EUR, USD, and GBP export receipts may be retained in commercial bank settlement accounts without mandatory repatriation timelines; however, transfer pricing, VAT, and Intrastat reporting obligations require arm's-length invoicing and contemporaneous records of the underlying cross-border e-commerce transactions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Cyprus Public Company Ltd

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: MEDIUM. Cyprus-licensed and EU-passported electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise Europe, Revolut Bank UAB, and Payhawk can open remote multi-currency accounts for a Cyprus Ltd; however, EMIs cannot provide statutory capital escrow services, bank guarantees, or traditional deposit accounts. PayPal and Shopify settlement should route to a mainstream credit institution to avoid payment-gateway scheme restrictions. EMI rails are suitable for operational sub-ledgers, FX conversion, and supplier disbursements but not for capital injections or tax-deposit holding.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Cyprus-resident directors may open accounts with a single physical branch visit or through bank-approved remote video onboarding supplemented by apostilled, notarized corporate documents and original passport verification. Non-resident directors and UBOs are generally required either to appear physically or to be verified through an internationally recognized notary, embassy consular officer, or prominent bank reference. Most tier-1 Cypriot banks retain discretion to mandate an in-person interview, and a Cyprus-registered corporate agent must sign the bank mandate when directors are unavailable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume inbound consumer payments from PayPal and Shopify webstore settlement with elevated chargeback ratios, triggering a source-of-revenue review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized passports, certificate of incorporation, shareholders register, UBO declaration, board resolution, certified e-commerce P&L, PayPal/Shopify transaction history, supplier invoices, shipment tracking logs, refund policy document, PCI-DSS compliance attestation, chargeback history, and EU Cosmetic Regulation (EC) 1223/2009 product notification files (CPNP codes).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO or a third-country corporate shareholder operating through an opaque ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed UBO declaration; notarized certificate of incorporation and good-standing certificate for each intermediate vehicle; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence for all natural-person UBOs; professional bank reference letter from the UBO's home institution; CV and biographical explanation of the Cyprus structure; any trust deed if nominee arrangements are disclosed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cosmetics trademark or counterfeit risk when the brand is newly registered or may infringe existing intellectual property.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EUIPO/WIPO trademark registration certificates, brand license or authorization letters from suppliers, manufacturer purchase contracts, product safety certificates and certificates of analysis, GMP compliance certifications, EU CPNP notifications, product liability insurance, and a documented recall/quality-incident procedure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cyprus tax residency ambiguity under the 60-day rule causing FATCA/CRS misreporting or management-and-control dispute.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cyprus Tax Department Tax Residency Certificate; board minutes and director attendance logs evidencing meetings held in Cyprus; employment contracts and GHS/social insurance registrations of Cyprus key personnel; CRS and FATCA self-certification forms; W-8BEN-E or W-9 documentation; correspondence with the Cyprus Registrar of Companies.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections and shareholder loans must arrive via SWIFT MT103 using the beneficiary bank's correct BIC/IBAN; field 70 must contain a BoP/IoP purpose text such as 'DIRECT INVESTMENT - EQUITY CAPITAL' or 'SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION'. The bank also requires a certified board resolution approving the share allotment, an updated share register, electronic filing with the Cyprus Registrar of Companies, and, for loans, a signed shareholder loan agreement with an arm's-length interest rate and repayment schedule. Capital received without consistent remittance references may be treated as unidentified funds and returned under AML procedures.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier and trade payments are executed via SWIFT MT103 for single cross-border transfers or MT101 files for batch runs; SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer are used for EU/EEA suppliers. For non-EEA cosmetics manufacturers, the bank may request purchase orders, proforma invoices, and the master supply contract; commercial letters of credit (MT700/MT707) are available if bulk import terms require them. Daily PayPal and Shopify settlement sweeps into the EUR operational account cover customer refunds and seller fees, with USD/GBP accounts used to reduce conversion friction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD FX forward (vanilla, under ISDA 2002 or bank standard Master FX Forward Agreement)
Deliverable EUR/GBP FX forward for UK webstore revenue hedges
European-style plain vanilla EUR/USD FX options, purchased premium only to avoid negative mark-to-market funding
Cross-currency swap (EUR/USD or EUR/GBP) for medium-term intercompany shareholder loan hedging, subject to EMIR trade reporting and margin obligations

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to currencies with legal convertibility restrictions (e.g., CNY, INR, TRY) executed under ISDA 1998 definitions; NDFs are not available for freely deliverable EUR pairs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies (DRCO) via Ariadne e-portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 30 June of each calendar year for all active Cyprus private limited companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalties of EUR 20 after two months and EUR 80 after five months; persistent non-payment leads to administrative strike-off of the company, with restoration obtainable through court order.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days following each anniversary of the company's date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Continuing offence under section 197 of the Companies Law; default fines of up to EUR 200 against the company and each officer, plus daily default fines and administrative strike-off risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies - Beneficial Owners Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June; also within 14 days after any change to beneficial ownership or shareholding structure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties up to EUR 200 per day for the company and its directors; continued violations may result in striking off and criminal liability for officers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March following the tax year end for calendar-year companies; electronically filed returns with audited financial statements may use the extended filing deadline of 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of EUR 100 per month or part thereof, capped at EUR 500; interest of 3% per annum on overdue tax; failure may trigger a tax assessment based on deemed income and criminal penalties for persistent evasion.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is always required for public interest entities, financial undertakings, and any company that does not qualify for the small company audit exemption under Section 69 of the Cyprus Companies Law. A private company qualifies for exemption if it satisfies at least two of the following three criteria in both the current and immediately preceding financial year: balance sheet total not exceeding EUR 350,000; net turnover not exceeding EUR 700,000; average number of employees not exceeding 5.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as endorsed by the EU is mandatory for audited companies; small and micro companies entitled to audit exemption may instead prepare financial statements under IFRS for SMEs or the local small-entity accounting framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Cyprus Companies Law requires every company to maintain an internal Beneficial Owners Register and separately file beneficial ownership data with the Registrar. Any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership must be reflected in the internal register and submitted to the Registrar within 14 days. Annually, the company must submit a confirmation that the stored UBO data is correct; this confirmation is particularly scrutinised where share transfers occurred during the year, and any mismatch is treated as a regulatory violation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (general meetings and directors' meetings)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% flat corporate income tax rate on the worldwide taxable income of Cyprus tax-resident companies; non-resident companies are taxed only on Cyprus-source income attributable to a permanent establishment.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory incentives applicable to a Cyprus cosmetics DTC retailer: (i) Notional Interest Deduction (NID) on new equity capital introduced after 1 January 2015, with the annual rate published by the Cyprus Minister of Finance (recent years ranging from 1.5% to 8%, e.g., 6.5% for 2023); (ii) 80% exemption for qualifying IP income (Cyprus IP Box for proprietary cosmetic brands, formulations and trademarks); (iii) 0% effective tax on qualifying dividend income received from Cyprus-resident and certain foreign companies under the participation exempt conditions; (iv) capital gains exemption except on gains from the disposal of Cyprus real estate and from trading in land; (v) 20% additional deduction for qualifying R&D expenditure; (vi) annual wear-and-tear capital allowances for IT infrastructure, e-commerce platforms and logistics equipment; (vii) unilateral double tax relief for foreign taxes borne on foreign-source income; (viii) group loss relief for Cyprus members of a 75% group.
